decision.about: what Page.Store needed to also serve Sidebar and LocalStorageSaver

options.say: add an `id` field Page.Store accepts instead of `page` - a caller with no page gets one fixed key, `prefix + id`, exactly matching Sidebar's old fixed `lew42:sidebar`

pull the guarded try/catch JSON.parse/stringify localStorage touch out as three static methods (read_raw/write_raw/clear_raw) any caller can use directly, even one that is not a Page.Store instance at all

decision.chose: both - id for Sidebar (needs Page.Store's get/patch shape), raw primitives for LocalStorageSaver (needs Saver's own load/write/delete contract with a real boolean, which Page.Store's always-silently-degrade contract does not give it)
decision.because: LocalStorageSaver could not just become `new Page.Store({id: this.key})` and call get/set - Saver.write() must report true failure (saver-panel-error-paths, 2026-08-15, proved UI depends on that), while Page.Store.set() deliberately never signals failure to its caller (a page keeps working when a save is lost). Two real contracts, one guarded primitive underneath both.
decision.rule: code#3 (a part is a class/method other classes can reach, not a second copy) + resolve-dont-park (the fence keeps ext/Ask/edit.js untouched, so LocalStorageSaver's file and class had to survive, not just its guts)

log.msg: item 2 done: Page.Store gained `id` (a caller with no page, one fixed key - Sidebar's rail) and three static raw primitives read_raw/write_raw/clear_raw (the guarded localStorage touch, used by both Page.Store itself and LocalStorageSaver). Sidebar.Store class deleted entirely (Sidebar.store() is now `new Page.Store({id: "sidebar"})`, same lew42:sidebar key). LocalStorageSaver.js kept as a file/class (ext/Ask/edit.js imports it, outside this task's fence) but its own guard code deleted, delegates to Page.Store's raw primitives. LINES: Sidebar.js store block 25->13 (-12, +1 import = -11 net), LocalStorageSaver.js whole file 44->25 (-19), Page.class.js Page.Store block 53->80 (+27, absorbing what both files leaned on). Net -3 across the three, well under the study's 20-25 estimate - the study costed deleting duplicate CODE (about 31 lines of hand-rolled guard across the two copies), not the line cost of writing the one place it now lives with this module's own documentation density; the duplicate logic really is gone, deleted for good, from two files down to one.

decision.about: how to seat ext/toc's rail inside ext/Doc's nested tabbed shell

options.say: add a NEW grid rule scoped to .doc-section in ext/Doc/Doc.css, duplicating toc.css's three-region template there

drop the `.pages >` ancestor-combinator from toc.css's two existing selectors, matching core/Page/Page.css's own .page:has(> .page-related) rule which never had that prefix and already reaches nested Doc pages today

decision.because: toc() actually renders inside catalog()'s own 'intro' child page (a real, separately-classed .page.page--intro), not directly inside .doc-section as first assumed - read Doc.js's overview_section()/catalog() before guessing. That intro child IS a .page, so `.page:has(> .toc)` (no ancestor constraint) already reaches it at ANY nesting depth, the exact same shape the related-aside rule already proved safe the same day. A second grid system in Doc.css would fight the first one on the SAME element two different ways instead of reusing the one that already works.
decision.rule: code#3 (reuse the part, do not duplicate it) - two lines changed, not a new rule

log.msg: item 3 done: toc.css's two grid selectors dropped their `.pages >` prefix (`.pages > .page:has(> .toc)` -> `.page:has(> .toc)`, and its `> .toc` seat rule the same way) - specificity (0,3,0) -> (0,2,0), still above the base .page rule's (0,1,0), matching Page.css's own .page:has(> .page-related) shape exactly. VERIFIED headless PORT=8143 at 1920: /framework/core/App/ and /framework/ext/markdown/ both draw a real rail now (3 links each, matching each page's own h2/h3 count) - the DOM has TWO .toc elements per nested Doc leaf (an ancestor index page's own, hidden by the ancestor's display:none once a deeper leaf is active - itself pre-existing, unrelated) and the leaf's real one nested inside catalog()'s 'intro' child page; picked the visible one by rect, not DOM order. Synthetic .page-related injected as a sibling of the visible toc (no real page has both yet): overlap=false, related falls into the main column ('folds under', same documented behavior Page.css already names for the plain-page case). At 1280 and 400 (below the 82em breakpoint) toc correctly stays display:none on both pages, zero regression, zero console errors. Bonus: re-crawled all 15 real toc() call sites - the 8 plain pages that already worked still work (specificity change is safe), and the other 5 Doc pages beyond the 2 the brief named (core/Router, core/Sidebar, ext/demo, ext/toc, util/markup) now ALSO draw a rail - all 15/15 now draw, not just 10.

assign.outcome:
**Three small fixes, all verified headless on a private server (port 8143).**

1. **The approved library's thumbnails.** `library_card()` assumed every browse item's jpeg lives at `/layouts/browse/shots/<id>-1920.jpg`; the five `approved-*` items carry their own `shot` field instead (a jpeg that predates `/layouts/browse/`). Now reads `entry.shot` first, same fallback `/layouts/browse/page.js`'s own `shot_url` already uses. Proof: a real Approve pressed on `/layouts/browse/approved-rail-content/`, zero failed image requests on the approved page afterward.
2. **One localStorage store.** `Page.Store` gained an `id` seam (a caller with no page, one fixed key) and three static guarded primitives (`read_raw`/`write_raw`/`clear_raw`). `Sidebar.Store` deleted outright — `Sidebar.store()` is `new Page.Store({ id: "sidebar" })` now, same `lew42:sidebar` key. `ext/Saver`'s `LocalStorageSaver` kept its file and class (`ext/Ask/edit.js` needs the Saver shape, outside this task's fence) but its own guard code is gone, delegating to the same three primitives. Proof: sidebar width and the shell rail both survive a reload under their existing keys, the Saver demo's 7 checks stay green, `/imagine/team/` and `/imagine/game/` round-trip under their expected keys unchanged.
3. **`ext/toc` inside `ext/Doc` pages.** The rail's grid selector required `.toc` to be a DIRECT child of a `.pages`-child `.page` — but a Doc module's toc lives inside `catalog()`'s own nested "intro" child page, several levels deep. Dropped the `.pages >` prefix from `toc.css`'s two selectors, matching `Page.css`'s own `.page:has(> .page-related)` rule, which never had that prefix. Proof: all 15 real `toc()` call sites now draw a rail (not just the 8 from this morning's fix) — `/framework/core/App/` and `/framework/ext/markdown/` checked at 1920 (rail draws, no overlap with a synthetic related aside), 1280 and 400 (no regression).
